roundSummary: Review round 1 requested two comment fixes in .github/workflows/ci.yaml, which the review App cannot push (GitHub refuses a GitHub App a workflow file without workflows permission). Both are made in commit f51c9b08: the job's comment now says why the document service runs under -race at all, and its cache comment no longer claims the job builds no binary. Both threads carry a disposition reply and are resolved; nothing else of the change moved.

proof.criterion: Review thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xva7v: the go-envoy cache comment claimed the job builds no binary, which a `go test -race` step does, so a later editor of the cache step would act on a false reason.
proof.surface: The pull request on GitHub: the thread, its disposition reply and its resolution, which is where the reviewer and the merger read a round's answer.
proof.command: gh api graphql -f query='mutation($t:ID!,$b:String!){addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(input:{pullRequestReviewThreadId:$t,body:$b}){comment{id}}}' -F t=PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xva7v -F b=<the reply>; then gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xva7v
proof.observed: The reply posted as PRRC_kwDORFy7ds8AAAABB07C0Q and the resolution answered isResolved true. The comment now reads, in the reviewer's own requested wording: 'go-envoy, restored only: its modules are the envoy module's, but this job builds the document service's race test binary, not the listener and natsd the family's saving jobs build, so it saves none.'
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer's own attempt is the control: GitHub refused the review App's push of this same file with 'refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/ci.yaml without workflows permission', which is why the edit is the implementer's and why a reviewer cannot close this class of finding itself.

proof.criterion: Review thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xva73: the job's comment said why the package has a job of its own but not why it runs under -race at all; that reason lived only in envoy-go-race's comment, whose direct test now runs here.
proof.surface: The same: the thread, its reply and its resolution on the pull request, and the comment in the workflow a later editor reads.
proof.command: The same two graphql calls with -F t=PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xva73 / -F id=PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xva73; and cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && grep -n 'func TestReadsOfALiveDocumentRunBesideItsPeers' packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/live_read_race_test.go
proof.observed: The reply posted as PRRC_kwDORFy7ds8AAAABB07EKg and the resolution answered isResolved true. The job comment now ends 'It runs under -race because a read that walks a live document without its lock races the room's peers, which no ordinary run shows (TestReadsOfALiveDocumentRunBesideItsPeers, internal/dispatch/docs/live_read_race_test.go:39, LEGION-499).' The grep answers '39:func TestReadsOfALiveDocumentRunBesideItsPeers(t *testing.T) {', so the citation names the right file and line. The sentence stays in envoy-go-race's comment as well, since it holds for the api package too.
proof.negativeControl: The line number is the part a comment gets wrong silently, so it was read rather than copied: the grep above prints line 39, and a citation of any other line would have printed a different number or nothing.

proof.criterion: Nothing else of the change moved: the router's gate still passes at the new head, and the job, its filter and its wiring are as the reviewer approved them.
proof.surface: The CI router's own gate program, .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.sh, what the ci-filters job runs, against the real .github/workflows/ci.yaml in the issue pod, plus the required lint step check-private-names.sh.
proof.observed: exit 0, with 'envoy-go-race: 2072 files, 0 uncovered (filter envoy_go_race)', 'envoy-go-race-docs: 755 files, 0 uncovered (filter envoy_go_race_docs)' and 'every ci.yaml filter matches every file its job reads (25 gates)' — the same numbers the tester and the reviewer read, which is what shows the two edits are comments and nothing else. check-private-names.sh green over 6279 files.
proof.negativeControl: The gate holds each job's pinned step name and run text in ci_job_reads.py to ci.yaml character for character, so an edit that strayed from a comment into a step name or a run line would have failed it; earlier in this issue the same command answered '27 gates' the moment two jobs were added, and 8 uncovered files the moment one filter pattern was deleted.

filesChanged: .github/workflows/ci.yaml: two comments of the envoy-go-race-docs job — the reason the package runs under -race, and what the go-envoy restore is for. No step, filter, timeout or wiring changed.
trickyParts: This class of finding can only be the implementer's: GitHub refuses a GitHub App a push that creates or updates a file under .github/workflows/ without the workflows permission, which the review App does not hold. A prose fix the reviewer would ordinarily make itself comes back as a changes request whenever it lands in a workflow file.
This round's push carries code, so it carries no skip-checks trailer and GitHub runs the router on it; the green run the body quotes was at 793974db, and the tester reads the new head's own run.
discoveredComplexity: Both findings were about a comment that had drifted from what the code does: one named a binary the job does not build, the other left the reason for -race in the job that no longer runs the test which proves it. Moving a package between jobs moves the reasons with it, and the reasons live in prose no gate reads.
